content.value_statement: Application errors often become inconsistent, noisy, or unsafe when each layer handles them differently. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward centralized handling, specific exceptions, safe messages, retries, and cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Identifies when to use centralized error handling in controllers, services, and API endpoints
Guides creation of specific exception classes for distinct error scenarios
Promotes user-friendly error messages that avoid technical detail exposure
Recommends graceful degradation and retry strategies for external service failures
Highlights cleanup of file handles, database connections, and other resources
limitations: Provides guidance only; it does not modify code without a separate user request
Does not include framework-specific implementation examples in the scanned skill file
Relies on a parent-directory markdown link that may be unavailable after packaging
Does not replace security review for sensitive logging and error disclosure decisions

use_cases.title: API Error Strategy
use_cases.description: Backend developers can standardize validation failures, service errors, and client responses across API endpoints.

use_cases.title: External Service Failures
use_cases.description: Platform engineers can plan retries, fallbacks, and user messaging when third-party services fail.

use_cases.title: Application Maintainability
use_cases.description: Tech leads can reduce scattered try-catch blocks and guide teams toward consistent error boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Review Basic Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this controller for error handling gaps. Suggest clearer exception types, safer user messages, and better cleanup points.

prompt_templates.title: Design Error Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design centralized error handling for a service and API layer. Include where errors should be caught, logged, and translated.

prompt_templates.title: Handle External Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Design error handling for calls to a payment provider. Include retry rules, graceful degradation, user-facing messages, and permanent failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Audit System Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this application's error handling strategy. Identify scattered catch blocks, unsafe messages, missing cleanup, and inconsistent transient versus permanent failure handling.

output_examples.input: A controller returns raw database error messages to users.
output: Replace raw technical details with a user-safe message.
Log the internal error with request context and sensitive data filtering.
Map database failures to a clear application exception at the service boundary.

output_examples.input: An integration sometimes times out when calling an external service.
output: Classify timeout failures as transient when retryable.
Use bounded retries with exponential backoff and clear stop conditions.
Provide a fallback path or degraded response when the service remains unavailable.

output_examples.input: A file import process leaves handles open after validation errors.
output: Add cleanup in a finalization path that always runs.
Validate preconditions before starting expensive work.
Return a user-friendly import failure message with a traceable support identifier.

best_practices: Use specific exception types so callers can handle known failure modes.
Log enough context for diagnosis while filtering secrets and user-sensitive data.
Centralize translation from internal errors to user-facing messages at application boundaries.
anti_patterns: Do not expose stack traces, database errors, or secret values to users.
Do not catch every exception in low-level code without preserving useful context.
Do not retry permanent failures or unbounded transient failures.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps design consistent error handling for services, controllers, API endpoints, retries, user messages, and cleanup.

faq.question: Does it write framework-specific code?
faq.answer: Not by itself. The scanned skill gives standards-level guidance that must be adapted to your framework.

faq.question: Can it help prevent information disclosure?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes user-friendly messages and logging practices that protect technical details and sensitive data.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when adding exception classes, try-catch blocks, retry logic, fail-fast checks, or centralized error handlers.

faq.question: Does it replace observability design?
faq.answer: No. It complements logging and monitoring design, but it does not define metrics, alerts, or tracing standards.

faq.question: What should I verify after using it?
faq.answer: Verify tests cover expected failures, user messages are safe, resources are closed, and retry behavior has limits.
